name: Coenzyme Q10
short: Few adverse events were reported in trials. A case report describes reduced warfarin response while taking CoQ10.
text: In a meta-analysis of 13 randomized trials of CoQ10 for fatigue, only one adverse (gastrointestinal) event was reported among 602 participants taking CoQ10, and a meta-analysis of 33 trials in heart failure reported no major adverse effects. A case report described a woman on warfarin whose response to warfarin fell while she took CoQ10 and returned when she stopped; the authors note CoQ10 is chemically similar to vitamin K and warn of possible warfarin treatment failure. This interaction evidence is from a case report.

quotes: A random effects model was implemented to conduct the meta-analysis among 13 RCTs (with a total of 1,126 participants).
There was only one adverse (gastrointestinal) event in the 602 participants who underwent the CoQ10 intervention.

citations.title: Effectiveness of Coenzyme Q10 Supplementation for Reducing Fatigue: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

quotes: In total, 33 studies were included in this meta-analysis
in those with heart failure without major adverse effects

citations.title: Efficacy and safety of coenzyme Q10 in heart failure: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

quotes: In the present case, a 72-year-old female treated with warfarin showed less responsiveness to warfarin than previously. It appeared she had taken coenzyme Q10, and when this was stopped, her responsiveness to warfarin was the same as before.
Coenzyme Q10 is chemically similar to K-vitamins, which may explain the interaction with warfarin.
Patients in treatment with warfarin should be aware of the possible risk of treatment failure when taking coenzyme Q10.
citations.label: Landbo et al., 1998, Ugeskr Laeger
citations.title: [Interaction between warfarin and coenzyme Q10].
